S, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA  ORAL ORDER Heard the learned counsel Sri.Mohan Kumar D., appearing for the petitioner, Sri.Rangaswamy R.,
the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for respondent No.1 and the learned counsel Sri.Vinod Kumar M., appearing for respondent No.2.
2.

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question the proceedings in C.C.No.18022/2023 for offences punishable under Sections 307, 498A, 506 and 201 read with Section 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
3. During the pendency of this petition, the parties to the lis have settled the dispute amongst themselves and drawn NC: 2024:KHC:44649 up a memorandum of settlement.

The settlement insofar as it germane to the present lis, reads as follows:
"9.

In view of the settlement arrived between the parties the parties have agreed to withdraw/quash/close the following cases as per the prevailing law of the land, they are:
a) The petitioner has filed Crime No.194/2022 Basaveshwaranagar Police Station,
Bengaluru which is pending before the 24th ACMM, Bengaluru.

b) The respondent has filed Crime No.191/2022 Wison Garden Police Station,
Bengaluru against the petitioner and his parents which is pending before the Narendra Devanga vs State Of Karnataka on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19965569/
2 VI-ACMM, Bengaluru and now numbered as S.C No.344/2024 on the file of City Civil and Sessions Judge, CCH-46, Bengaluru.
c) The respondent has filed C.Misc No.40/2023 against the petitioner and his parents which is pending before III MMTC, Bengaluru and also filed Crl.A.No.694/2023 and Crl.A No.454/2024 on the file of the City Civil and Sessions Judge, CCH-67,
Bengaluru,
d) The respondent has filed O.S. No.7553/2022 against the petitioner and her father pending on the file of the City Civil and Sessions Judge, CCH-3, Bengaluru.
e) Both the parties have agreed to co-operate to close WP.No.21588/2023 and W.P.No.21568/2023 pending before the Hon'ble High Karnataka, Bengaluru and get the offences compounded and close the cases respectively."
4.
An application for compounding in the light of the settlement is also filed and the same is taken on record.
The other offence alleged against the accused is the one punishable under Section 307 of the IPC.
Since it is the offence of attempt to murder, the compounding of the offences would generally not arise.

The Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Laxmi Narayan and others reported in (2019)5 SCC 688, while taking note of the fact has held that the offence under Section 307 of the IPC should not result in the Court exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., to dismiss the application seeking compounding of the offence only in cases where the wound certificate would depict to be grievous in nature and the would inflicted on vital parts.

sentences.text: 6. The case at hand is the offence of attempt to murder between the husband and the wife.
Therefore, I deem it appropriate to accept the application for compounding between the parties and compound the offences.

7. In the light of the settlement arrived at between the parties and the offences not being against the State, I deem it NC: 2024:KHC:44649 appropriate to accept the same and terminate the proceedings, qua the petitioner.
8. For the aforesaid reasons, the petition is disposed.
The proceedings in C.C.No.18022/2023 pending on the file of the VI Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, qua the petitioner, stand quashed.
